newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: JCI chairman says Lonrho in bag - report.
newsitem.headline: JCI chairman says Lonrho in bag - report.

text.p: JCI Ltd Chairman Mzi Khumalo said in a newspaper interview on Thursday that JCI would take possession of more than 27 percent of British conglomerate Lonrho Plc shares in November.
"It's done, it's sealed and it's going ahead. We have already acquired the shares and we will take delivery in November," Khumalo told Zimbabwe's Financial Gazette.
JCI announced on July 2 it would buy a 26.8 percent stake in Lonrho previously held by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd for around 2.5 billion rand ($531.6 million).
JCI on Wednesday officially notified the London Stock Exchange that it held options on 217,909,683 Lonrho shares. If taken up, it will give JCI a 27.6 percent stake in Lonrho.
The South African company said last Friday it planned to issue a circular to shareholders relating to its planned acquisition of a 26.8 percent interest in Lonrho.
It said the circular would be forwarded in sufficient time to allow for a general shareholder meeting to be convened to approve the deal before November 20 1997.
Khumalo told the newspaper that JCI ultimately aims to hold a stake of around 30 percent in Lonrho.
JCI officials in Johannesburg were not immediately available for comment.
